paragraphs: There is an opinion that public museums and art galleries will no longer be necessary as people can use a computer to see historical objects and works of art. From my perspective, I am of the opposite school of thought.

Admittedly, technology makes cultural and historical experiences more accessible. Firstly, people can use high-resolution images; three-dimensional reconstructions; virtual reality platforms on their computers to explore masterpieces and ancient artefacts in remarkable detail without leaving home. For example, the Louvre museum in France provides online tours, allowing art lovers around the world to explore famous artwork from home. This is especially useful for people who cannot afford to travel or have mobility issues; they can still access a vast range of cultural and historical heritages.

However, I strongly believe that public museums and art galleries are still necessary. Initially, online experience cannot replicate the direct sensory engagement of seeing an artefact or artwork in person. Real experience can evoke emotions and a sense of authenticity that digital images cannot convey. For example, when people visit a museum and see objects from a war, they may feel more sympathy for people who suffered and died during that war. Furthermore, museums and galleries are vital cultural hubs that symbolize the identity of a region. This cultural role can attract tourists and help people bond within the community.

In conclusion, computers provide a convenient way to access historical heritages and artworks. I am firmly convinced that museums and art galleries remain important places that offer direct experiences and bring communities together.

review.title: Nhận xét bài viết trên lớp
paragraphs: There is an opinion that dangerous sports should be prohibited by law, while others think individuals should be free to participate in them. This essay will dicuss both news before explaining why I support the latter opinion, provided that certain conditions are met.

Admittedly, one might argue that dangerous sports should be prohibited is true. The most important one is that even a minor error can lead to serious injuries or even death. For example, activities such as skydiving and bungee jumping. However this ban has two drawbacks; firstly, these activities often take place in remote locations, say mountain cliffs, thus, there is limited minimal surveillance or control. Secondly, it is unrealistic to appear a police officer follows every individuals participating in these sport. As a result, exist only on paper, people may continue practising the underground, it harder to ensure basic safety standards.

On the other hand, I believe people should be permitted to do any sport, as long as they understand risks and receive sufficient training. For instance, activities such as deep-ocean diving or bungee jumping should join reputable clubs that provide appropriate equipment and qualified supervision. Furthermore, beginners also should be accompanied by an expert and taught what to do when accident occur recognise dangers and respond appropriately. Overall, proper training and necessary precautions are safer participation but no activity is entirely risk-free.
In conclusion, banning dangerous sports is neither practical nor effective freedom to choose, under strict conditions of training and awareness, this would be a more realistic approach.

review.overall: Em giữ được hai quan điểm và kết luận ủng hộ tự do có điều kiện; những ý chính về nơi xa, cảnh sát, câu lạc bộ và chuyên gia đều có mặt. Tuy vậy, câu ví dụ Body 1 là mảnh câu, câu hệ quả thiếu chủ ngữ, và Body 2 gán hành động ‘join clubs’ cho các môn thể thao thay vì người tham gia. Em cần viết lại các ý đó thành câu đủ chủ–vị và kiểm tra chủ thể làm hành động trước khi nối ý.

paragraphs: There is an opinion that dangerous sports should be prohibited by law, while others think individuals should be free to participate in them. This essay will discuss both views before explaining why I support the latter opinion, provided that certain conditions are met.

Admittedly, one might argue that dangerous sports should be prohibited. Their main reason is that even a minor error can lead to serious injuries or death. For example, skydiving and bungee jumping can cause serious accidents. However, this ban has two drawbacks. Firstly, these activities often take place in remote locations, such as mountain cliffs, where surveillance or control is limited. Secondly, it is unrealistic to expect a police officer to follow every individual participating in these sports. As a result, a ban may exist only on paper and people may continue practising these sports underground, making basic safety standards harder to ensure.

Instead, I believe people should be permitted to do any sport as long as they understand the risks and receive sufficient training. For instance, people who want to try deep-ocean diving or bungee jumping should join reputable clubs that provide appropriate equipment and qualified supervision. Furthermore, beginners should also be accompanied by an expert and taught what to do when accidents occur, enabling them to recognise dangers and respond appropriately. Overall, proper training and necessary precautions make participation safer, although no activity is entirely risk-free.
In conclusion, banning dangerous sports is neither practical nor effective. Freedom to choose under strict conditions of training and awareness is a more realistic approach.

review.title: Nhận xét bài viết trên lớp
paragraphs: There is an opinion that children should be allowed to learn through trial and errors, while others think that parents need to protect their children from making mistake. From my perspective, I children should be encouraged to make mistakes, provided that errors do not involve serious danger.

Admittedly, opponents of trial-and-error approach often emphasize that most mistake are avoidable. For example, children do not need to get hurt by knives, fire or electricity to learn to be careful. Moreover, parents have a duty to shield their children from harm and forestall mistake, believing that it help them fulfil this duty. When parents pre-emptively help children, it brings them peace of mind knowing that they are doing their best to protect and raise their child.

However, those on the other side have their own valid reasoning. Firstly, parents cannot be around all the time, making it inevitable that children will experiment with new things and make mistakes. Through these experiences, children gain invaluable lessons that will stand children in good stead in later stages of life. Conversely, if children be shielded from everything, they risk grow up overdependent on others, which is an undesirable trait for their personal development.

Overall, it seems to me that parents should allow children to learn from mistakes to prepare for future, provided that parents intervene or give guidance on important matters to prevent errors that may derail their future.

review.overall: Em bám sát dàn ý: ba nhánh của phe ngăn sai lầm, ba nhánh của phe cho trẻ thử sai và ngoại lệ ở kết luận đều có. Hai Body chuyển ý khá rõ. Em cần sửa những chỗ “it help” và “they risk grow up” để chia động từ và cấu trúc đúng. Câu “it brings them peace of mind” có quy chiếu rõ về việc cha mẹ giúp con và cảm giác của cha mẹ, nên giữ. Câu mở có một chữ I gạch chưa chắc, nên cô không tính nét ấy là lỗi.

task.text:
WRITING TASK 1
You should spend about 20 minutes on this task.
The graph below shows the three different kinds of emission sources (oil/coal/gas) of greenhouse gas in the UK.
Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
Write at least 150 words.

images.alt: Biểu đồ khí thải từ oil, coal và gas tại Anh, 1990–2010

paragraphs: The given bar chart illustrates how much emissions were produced by greenhouse gas sources, including coal, gas, oil, in the UK over a 20-year period, commencing from 1990.

Overall, there was a general increase in the amount of fossil fuels for gas over the timeline, whereas the opposite was true for those generated by oil and coal. Also of note is that the figures for gas sources recorded the highest figures in the end period of time.

To elaborate, approximately 310 million tons of coal were recorded in 1990 and decrease to 250 million tons in 2000. The figures for oil and gas witnessing a lower number, with around 270 million tons of oil emissions in 1990 and declined by 10 millions tons after 10 years, and with 220 million tons of gas sources increase to 300 million tons at the same period of time.

Regarding the latter, the amounts of fossil fuels for gas experienced an upward, increasing by 20 million tons over the next decade, ranked first on the entire chart. By contrast, the figures for oil and coal declined sharply, falling to nearly 50 and 60 million tons respectively from 2000 to 2010.
review.overall: Em nhìn ra ba xu hướng chính và gas đứng đầu vào cuối kỳ. Cần giữ đúng đại lượng là lượng khí thải, rồi viết rõ 50 và 60 triệu tấn là mức giảm chứ không phải giá trị cuối. Em cũng cần rút ngắn các câu chứa nhiều số liệu để người đọc theo kịp.

criteria.comment: Em nêu đúng chiều tăng của gas và giảm tổng thể của oil, coal, cùng vị trí gas cao nhất ở cuối. Tuy nhiên em nhiều lần đổi đại lượng carbon emissions thành lượng fossil fuels; câu cuối nói các số liệu giảm xuống 50 và 60 triệu tấn, không phải mức giảm của chúng.

criteria.label: CC
criteria.comment: Bài có mở bài, tổng quan và hai đoạn chi tiết theo thời gian. Trong từng đoạn, chuỗi câu dài nối nhiều ý làm quan hệ giữa số đầu, số cuối và độ chênh chưa rõ.

criteria.label: LR
criteria.comment: Có từ mô tả xu hướng và so sánh, nhưng các cụm “fossil fuels for gas”, “experienced an upward” và “gas sources” không chuẩn cho lượng phát thải.

criteria.label: GRA
criteria.comment: Nhiều cấu trúc động từ sai hoặc thiếu động từ chính, chẳng hạn “figures ... witnessing” và “gas ... increase”; vẫn nhận ra phần lớn số liệu và ý chính.

paragraphs.text: The bar chart compares carbon emissions from gas, oil and coal in the UK between 1990 and 2010. The quantities are measured in millions of tons.

Overall, emissions from gas rose throughout the period, becoming the largest of the three sources from 2000 onwards. Coal emissions declined steadily, while oil emissions were lower at the end than at the beginning despite a temporary increase in 2000.

In 1990, coal produced approximately 310 million tons of emissions, compared with around 270 million tons from oil and 220 million tons from gas. Five years later, gas had risen to about 270 million tons, almost matching coal at roughly 280 million tons. Oil, meanwhile, had fallen to approximately 240 million tons. By 2000, gas had climbed further to 300 million tons and overtaken both other sources. At that point, oil and coal emitted about 260 and 250 million tons, respectively.

Over the following decade, gas emissions increased by around 20 million tons to reach 320 million tons in 2010. In contrast, oil fell by approximately 50 million tons to 210 million tons, and coal declined by about 60 million tons to 190 million tons. Coal was therefore the smallest source at the end of the period.

review.title: Task 2 · History, science and technology

pages.alt: Bài Task 2 viết tay của TRIỆU PHƯƠNG DUNG, trang 1
Bài Task 2 viết tay của TRIỆU PHƯƠNG DUNG, trang 2

task.text:
WRITING TASK 2
You should spend about 40 minutes on this task.
Some people say history is one of the most important school subjects. Other people think that, in today’s world, subjects like science and technology are more important than history. Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.
Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your knowledge or experience.
Write at least 250 words.

paragraphs: There is an opinion that schools should give more importance to History than others subjects while others think in modern's world, Science and Technology are more important than History. From my perspective, I believe that both equally necessary and should be given similar attention in schools.

On the one hand, Science and Technology play a role in today's digital world. Firstly, technological developments can promote economic growth and create many well-paid job opportunities in fields such as computer science, engineering and medicine. Secondly, scientific knowledge is needed to solve major global issues, such as climate change, pollution and diseases. Therefore, focusing on these subjects can help students prepare for a modern workforce and contribute to nation's development, which are necessary in both economic and future careers.

On the other hand, learning History also provides essential benefits that technical subjects cannot offer. Initially, History teaches students critical thinking skills by helping them analyse past events and make careful judgements. For example, learning about past can help people understand current problems and avoid repeating mistakes such as wars or bad policies, decline economic. Furthermore, studying History helps students understanding their culture and heritage, which can strengthen their connection with society, help young people know how societies changed over time.

In conclusion, I believe that both History and Science, Technology are equally valuable. While Science and Technology are important in today's digital, History helps students understand about life in the past and the today's world.
review.overall: Em có bố cục rõ và ý kiến cân bằng nhất quán. Hai đoạn thân chọn được lợi ích phù hợp cho từng nhóm môn; để bài thuyết phục hơn, em cần triển khai một ví dụ cụ thể thay vì chỉ kể tên nhiều lợi ích. Đồng thời sửa các câu thiếu động từ và dùng sai dạng từ.

criteria.label: TR
criteria.comment: Em thảo luận hai quan điểm và giữ ý kiến hai nhóm môn đều cần thiết. Các lý do về nghề nghiệp, vấn đề toàn cầu, tư duy và di sản đều phù hợp; ví dụ vẫn ở mức liệt kê, chưa cho thấy một trường hợp cụ thể làm ý nổi bật.

criteria.label: CC
criteria.comment: Bốn đoạn rõ, mỗi thân bài phụ trách một nhóm môn và kết luận khép lại lập trường. Một số câu cuối đoạn ghép nhiều hệ quả bằng dấu phẩy làm mạch giải thích kém gọn.

criteria.label: LR
criteria.comment: Từ vựng theo chủ đề khá đa dạng: economic growth, pollution, critical thinking, heritage. Một số cụm dùng chưa chính xác như “modern’s world”, “decline economic”, “today’s digital”.

criteria.label: GRA
criteria.comment: Có nhiều câu phức hiểu được, nhưng lỗi thiếu động từ, hòa hợp và dạng từ xuất hiện xuyên bài: “both equally necessary”, “helps students understanding”, “History helps student”.

annotations.quote: modern's world
annotations.title: Sở hữu cách không phù hợp
annotations.explanation: Viết “the modern world” hoặc “today’s world”; “modern” không phải danh từ sở hữu trong cụm này.
annotations.replacement: the modern world

annotations.quote: both equally necessary
annotations.title: Thiếu động từ to be
annotations.explanation: Chủ ngữ “both” cần “are” trước tính từ “equally necessary”.
annotations.replacement: both are equally necessary

annotations.quote: climate change, pollution and diseases
annotations.title: Phát triển một ví dụ
annotations.explanation: Ba vấn đề đều liên quan, nhưng em mới liệt kê; chọn một vấn đề rồi giải thích kiến thức khoa học giúp xử lý nó như thế nào.
annotations.replacement: climate change, for example, by helping researchers develop cleaner sources of energy

annotations.quote: decline economic
annotations.title: Sai dạng và trật tự từ
annotations.explanation: Nếu nêu hậu quả chính sách xấu, dùng “economic decline”; cần nối rõ với câu trước.
annotations.replacement: economic decline

annotations.quote: helps students understanding
annotations.title: Động từ sau help
annotations.explanation: Sau “help + someone”, dùng động từ nguyên mẫu “understand”.
annotations.replacement: helps students understand

annotations.quote: today's digital
annotations.title: Thiếu danh từ
annotations.explanation: “Digital” là tính từ và cần danh từ đi sau, ví dụ “digital world”.
annotations.replacement: today's digital world

annotations.quote: others subjects
annotations.title: Others trước danh từ
annotations.explanation: Trước danh từ “subjects”, dùng “other”, không dùng đại từ “others”.
annotations.replacement: other subjects

annotations.quote: contribute to nation's development
annotations.title: Thiếu mạo từ sở hữu
annotations.explanation: Cần “their nation’s development” hoặc “a nation’s development”.
annotations.replacement: contribute to their nation's development

annotations.quote: learning about past
annotations.title: Thiếu the trước past
annotations.explanation: Khi “past” là danh từ chỉ quá khứ, dùng “the past”.
annotations.replacement: learning about the past

annotations.quote: which can strengthen their connection with society, help young people know how societies changed over time
annotations.title: Hai vế sau which chưa song song
annotations.explanation: Vế này nối hai tác dụng của việc học lịch sử; thêm “and” trước “help” và giữ cả hai động từ song song.
annotations.replacement: which can strengthen their connection with society and help young people understand how societies have changed over time

annotations.quote: understand about life in the past and the today's world
annotations.title: Giới từ và mạo từ ở kết luận
annotations.explanation: “Understand” nhận tân ngữ trực tiếp; bỏ “about”. “Today’s world” không thêm “the”.
annotations.replacement: understand life in the past and today's world

paragraphs.text: Schools must decide how much attention to give history compared with science and technology. Some people regard history as a particularly important subject, while others favour technical fields in the modern world. I believe that both deserve substantial attention because they prepare students for different aspects of life.

Science and technology are crucial to economic development and the challenges society faces today. Technology classes can help students learn digital skills that employers increasingly seek in fields such as engineering and medicine. Scientific knowledge also helps people address major problems. For example, researchers can use an understanding of climate change to develop cleaner sources of energy and reduce pollution. Students who study these subjects can therefore prepare for a wide range of careers while gaining the tools to contribute to their communities. This is a strong reason to keep science and technology prominent in the curriculum.

History offers benefits that technical subjects cannot provide in the same way. Studying past events teaches students to examine evidence, consider different accounts and make careful judgments. Learning about a failed policy, for instance, can show them how decisions may cause economic decline and affect ordinary people. History also introduces students to the people, traditions and events that shaped their country. This knowledge can strengthen their sense of belonging and help them understand present-day debates. A school that taught only technical skills would leave students with fewer opportunities to explore these social and cultural questions.

In conclusion, science and technology can equip students for modern work and help them respond to global problems, whereas history develops historical judgment and cultural understanding. I therefore think schools should teach both areas well, rather than treating either one as unnecessary.
